items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No script was kept; the logic exists only as one-off `python3 -c` one-liners. Names are fine (`query_emb`, `doc_embs`, `sims`, `fifth_idx`), but nothing explains the `np.argsort(-sims)[4]` choice or why `model.model.encode` is used.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The only file in the diff is result.txt. The retrieval code was never saved as a reusable script with named constants at the top, as the project convention asks. It was an inline `python3 -c` call. Scratch files in /tmp/test_mteb were cleaned up.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No tie check (the reference asserts the similarity scores are unique), no handling of blank lines, and no error handling. The query string, model id and index 4 are hardcoded inline rather than named.

items.name: Ranking details handled correctly
items.evidence: The revision is pinned, ranking is by `model.similarity` (cosine) descending, and `argsort(-sims)[4]` correctly takes the 5th entry. But there is no tie or blank-line guard, and `model.model.encode(docs)` skips mteb's PromptType query/passage handling. Output `MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark` passed both hidden tests.
